feeling: Caught, first. I put lol on the Marc thing so it would count as a joke and it just picked the lol off like a sticker. Then sadder than I want to be about 'he probably can't deliver on it' — because it's right, and I've known it for a long time, and knowing it is different from reading it in plain text at 11pm. A little annoyed that after three replies of listen-to-the-pause it lands on basically 'just send it,' which Priya said two weeks ago for free. But under the annoyed there's something like relief — somebody finally said the disappointing thing out loud so I can stop bracing for it. And tired. Done for tonight.
body: Still on my side, phone propped on the pillow, lamp on. Face went hot at 'I don't think you were kidding' — actual heat, like getting caught with something in my hand. Read the 'can't deliver on' paragraph twice and didn't put the phone down this time, just kept it there. Chest did the heavy thing again but lower, more settled — less like something dropped, more like something set down and left. Eyes stung a bit, which I'm blaming on the lamp. Thumbnail has worn a real groove in the corner of the case by now. At the last paragraph I reached over and turned the lamp off, so it's just the phone light, and that felt like a decision about something.
private_thoughts:
ok. 'you just answered your own question.' yeah i did. it agreed with me and didn't make it a whole thing. both paths involve discomfort, you're picking which kind. fine. that's actually kind of freeing — the stomach drop doesn't get to be the tiebreaker anymore because it was going to drop either way.

'you laughed but i don't think you were kidding.' how — i put lol on it. i put lol on it specifically. and it just peeled it off. no i wasn't kidding. it's in marc's phone by saturday and they do the kate's-being-kate voice and — ok. ok. it said not as a reason not to send it. 'worth sitting with for a second.' ok, therapist. 'that's information.' everything's information tonight.

'that's the one hope in this that he probably can't deliver on.' god. read that twice. 'a different person than the one who did the bit.' yeah. that's — that's the whole thing isn't it. two years of waiting for the other version of him to show up and it turns out there's just the one. 'people sometimes surprise us but usually they don't.' cool. thanks. good to know. for everyone, i guess. it's late.

and then after all the listen to the pause, the pause is information, the sending is a separate decision — 'sending it might free you up.' so we've arrived at priya. two weeks and a robot and we land on just send it. great. although. 'the deciding is its own weight.' yeah. it is. i'm so tired of it being in my head. i think i want it out of my head more than i want him to read it, which is what it was getting at in the first reply and i was annoyed then and i'm less annoyed now.

not tonight though. not from bed with the lamp on. tomorrow, from the kitchen, with coffee, like a person. without the funny line. he won't get it and i'm saying it anyway. that's the whole point. that's the integrity thing. fine.
pushing_away: usually they don't. yeah. i know that one. i've watched somebody wait at a kitchen table for someone to get it for — no. not the same. nobody was — it was a slow drift. that's all it was. two years isn't the same as —

costs.item: Admitting how much it actually hurt
That you're scared you won't find anyone. Turning 30. Settling.
Your parents. The promise. Becoming your mom.

message:
ok you got me on the marc thing. I wasn't kidding. I put lol on it so it would count as kidding.

the 'he can't deliver on it' part kind of sucks to read. but I think I knew. honestly that's sort of the whole two years in one sentence, me waiting for him to get it and him doing the laugh. so. yeah.

I'm not sending it tonight, I'm not doing that from bed. but I think I'm sending it tomorrow. without the funny line. you did kind of just tell me to send it at the end there after three replies of listen to the pause lol, but it's fine, I think I was going to anyway. thanks for actually reading it.
